subject: Genetics
title: Base Editing
description: A fast breakdown of Base Editing for builders.

hook.text: What if you could change one DNA letter without cutting both strands? Base editing does exactly that.

buildup.text: David Liu's lab fused a deactivated Cas9 to a chemical that converts one base into another. C becomes T. A becomes G.

discovery.text: Base editors fix point mutations—the most common cause of genetic disease. One letter, one change, one cure.

twist.text: No double-strand break means fewer errors. Base editing is safer than classic CRISPR for single-letter diseases.

climax.text: In 2022, base editing treated a girl's incurable leukemia. Her cancer-fighting cells were edited to attack the tumor.

punchline.text: Sometimes fixing one letter is enough to save a life.

quiz.question: What makes base editing different from standard CRISPR?
options: It changes single letters without cutting
